entries.model: v²=v₀²+2as; x=v₀t+at²/2
derivation: The physical root for 1500 m is t_T=73.1790 s, hence t_car=63.1790 s.
For the car, a=2(1200-(40/3.6)t)/t² and v_C=40/3.6+at.

entries.model: Relative displacement equals the two vehicle lengths and both 20 m gaps.
derivation: Required relative gain: 20+4.5+20+2.5=47 m.
Acceleration for 4 s gains 10 m; braking for 2 s gains 5 m; the remaining 32 m at 5 m/s takes 6.4 s.

entries.model: Piecewise constant-acceleration kinematics.
derivation: The graphs are piecewise: a={2,6}; v is continuous linear; x is continuous quadratic.
entries.result: t_AC=8.1236 s; v_C=26.8328 m/s; graph construction specified

entries.model: Police accelerates to its cap, then closes the remaining gap at constant relative speed.
derivation: Car speed is 33.3333 m/s; police cap is 41.6667 m/s and is reached after 8.3333 s of police motion.
At that instant the gap is 204.1667 m; closing it at 8.3333 m/s takes 24.5 s.
entries.result: t=35.8333 s after the car passes; x=1194.44 m

entries.model: Choose east as positive; the truck decelerates, so a=-0.6 m/s². Use x=v₀t+at²/2 and v=v₀+at.
derivation: For the truck over AB: 180=10v₀+(-0.6)·10²/2, so v₀=21 m/s.
At the meeting after 4 s, the truck has covered x_m=21·4+(-0.6)·4²/2=79.2 m; the car covers 180-79.2=100.8 m, so its speed magnitude is 25.2 m/s west.
The truck speed at the meeting is v_m=21+(-0.6)·4=18.6 m/s east.
entries.result: truck v₀=21 m/s, v_B=15 m/s; car=25.2 m/s west; truck at meeting=18.6 m/s east
entries.comparison_note: Owner-authorized visual review of the handwritten solution confirms the sign convention and all four answer-key values.

entries.model: Locked-wheel deceleration a=-μg; average power W/t.
derivation: F_f=μmg=6621.75 N and P_avg=F_f d/t.

entries.model: The sum of the two covered distances is 500 m.
derivation: Substitution into each motion equation gives the two meeting distances and speeds.

entries.model: Three phases: accelerate, cruise, then brake to the next station.
derivation: To 20 m/s at 0.4 m/s²: t₁=50 s and x₁=500 m; 15 min cruise gives x₂=18000 m.
Ordinary braking at -0.4 m/s² needs 500 m, overshooting the 19000 m station spacing by 100 m.
To stop in 400 m requires a=-0.5 m/s² and t₃=40 s.
entries.result: station spacing=19000 m; corrected total time=990 s

entries.model: Piecewise bus motion plus relative walking during braking.
derivation: The bus reaches 14 m/s in 7 s, so a=2 m/s² and covers 49 m; 5 min cruise adds 4200 m.
Stopping over 50 m gives a=-1.96 m/s² and t=7.1429 s.
The walker must gain 30 m in that time from 2 m/s: 30=2t+at²/2.
entries.result: x_AB=4299 m; total time=314.143 s=5.236 min; walker a=0.616 m/s²

entries.model: Use one origin and a common clock; vehicle A starts 14 s before vehicle B.
derivation: Let τ be the time after B starts; A then travels for τ+14. Coordinate equality gives 10τ+τ²/2=15(τ+14), or τ²-10τ-420=0.
D=(-10)²-4·1·(-420)=1780. The roots are (10±√1780)/2; the negative root is rejected, giving τ=26.095 s.
Elapsed time after A starts is 40.095 s. B speed is 10+τ=36.095 m/s, above 120 km/h=33.333 m/s.
The meeting coordinate is x=15·40.095=601.42 m; substitution in B's equation gives the same coordinate.
entries.comparison_note: Owner and owner-authorized handwritten review confirm the repository solution. The answer key is wrong only in part ג: it uses B-relative time for A's distance and reports 391.42 m instead of 601.42 m.

entries.model: Vertical motion y=v₀t-gt²/2 with origin at the wall top.
derivation: At t=3 s the stone is 6 m below launch: -6=3v₀-9.81·3²/2, hence v₀=12.715 m/s.
Rise above the wall is v₀²/(2g)=8.241 m; impact velocity is v₀-g·3=-16.715 m/s.
The descending crossing of wall-top height is at 2v₀/g=2.592 s, leaving 0.408 s to impact.
entries.result: v₀=12.715 m/s; maximum height above ground=14.241 m; impact speed=16.715 m/s; t₂=0.408 s

entries.model: Vertical motion from a platform 5 m above water.
derivation: Maximum height above water is 5+v₀²/(2g)=5.825 m and impact velocity v₀-g·1.5=-10.691 m/s.
For v₀=2 m/s, the positive root of -5=2t-gt²/2 is 1.234 s.
entries.result: v₀=4.024 m/s; H_max=5.825 m; v_f=-10.691 m/s; alternate t=1.234 s

entries.model: Both balls have equal launch speed; the second is launched when the first reaches its apex.
derivation: The printed 5 m rise with g=9.81 gives v₀=√(2g·5)=9.9045 m/s and launch delay v₀/g=1.00964 s.
After the second launch, equality 5-gt²/2=v₀t-gt²/2 gives t=5/v₀=0.50482 s.
Meeting height above the floor is 1+5-gt²/2=4.750 m.
entries.result: v₀=9.9045 m/s; delay=1.00964 s; meet after second launch=0.50482 s; height=4.750 m
entries.comparison_note: Owner review confirms the repository solution and the handwritten solution are correct. All four answer-key values conflict with the printed 5 m rise and g=9.81 m/s².

entries.model: Horizontal release: x=v_xt and H=gt²/2.
derivation: The sight angle satisfies tanβ=240/x.

entries.model: Horizontal release from 8 m.
derivation: Horizontal distance L=10t=12.771 m; a relaxed release has the same vertical fall time.

entries.model: The package inherits helicopter horizontal speed; compare with the bus during free fall.
derivation: Fall time from 720 m is t=√(1440/9.81)=12.116 s.
Closing speed is 270/3.6+90/3.6=100 m/s, so release separation is 1211.6 m and separation at impact is zero.
At impact v_x=75 m/s left and v_y=gt=118.85 m/s down.
entries.result: x=1211.6 m; Δx=0; |v|=140.53 m/s; direction=57.7° below horizontal

entries.model: Energy on the frictionless roof, then projectile motion from B.
derivation: From B, -9=-v_B sin37°·t-gt²/2 gives t=0.892 s.
v_x=v_B cos37°, v_y=-v_B sin37°-gt; d=v_xt.

entries.model: Accelerated sliding with friction, then oblique downward projectile motion.
derivation: From height 2.5 m, -2.5=-v_C sin30°·t-gt²/2 gives t=0.471 s.
Resolve the impact components and use R=v_C cos30°·t.

entries.model: Sliding with friction through a 5 m vertical drop, then projectile motion to a 1.5 m platform.
derivation: a_s=g(sin37°-0.2cos37°); path AB=5/sin37°, giving v_B=8.72 m/s.
The projectile drops 10-1.5=8.5 m: -8.5=-v_B sin37°·t-gt²/2, giving t=0.887 s.
Horizontal reach is a=v_B cos37°·t.

entries.model: A free-falls 5 m while B travels 8.66 m horizontally.
derivation: t=√(10/9.81)=1.010 s and v_B0=8.66/t=8.574 m/s (rounding of the printed distance controls the last digits).
If A is instead thrown downward at the same speed, solve 5=v_B0·t+gt²/2 for the required delay.
entries.result: fall time≈1.010 s; horizontal launch≈8.58 m/s; delay≈0.461 s

entries.model: Uniform deceleration on ice; then horizontal projectile motion.
derivation: At 5 m/s with a=-0.5 m/s², stopping time is 10 s and stopping distance 25 m, so the stone does not reach B at 30 m.
The minimum initial speed satisfies v₀²=2·0.5·30, hence 5.477 m/s and stop time 10.954 s.
For a 5 m horizontal throw, t=√(10/9.81) and v₀=30/t.
entries.result: t_stop=10 s; x_stop=25 m; v_min=5.477 m/s; corresponding t=10.954 s; throw speed=29.714 m/s

entries.model: C is the apex: y=gt²/2 and x=v_xt.
Equal-height projectile range R=v₀²sin(2α)/g.
derivation: Rise h=(v₀sin55°)²/(2g)=2.856 m.

entries.model: Use the supplied projectile equations at the basket coordinate.
derivation: At x=9 m, y rises from 2.1 m to 3.0 m; solving y-y₀=x tan30°-gx²/(2v₀²cos²30°) gives v₀≈11.1 m/s.
Substitution at player B, x=7.5 m, gives the ball height.
entries.result: v₀≈11.1 m/s; height over B≈3.447 m

entries.model: Projectile launched 30° upward from height 1.4 m with total flight 1.65 s.
derivation: L=v_Acos30°·1.65 and h_max=1.4+(v_Asin30°)²/(2g).

entries.model: At the apex after 8000 m horizontally, v_y=0.
derivation: For a 45° launch, x_apex=u²/(2g), so u=√(2g·8000)=396.18 m/s.
Rise is u²/(4g)=4000 m, hence H=4600 m.
Solve 0=600+u sin45°·t-gt²/2 and use R=u cos45°·t.

entries.model: Energy along the smooth plane, then projectile motion from a 1.5 m height.
derivation: v_B=√(10²-2g·1.5)=8.4006 m/s; the launch angle is arctan(1.5/2)=36.87°.
The ballistic rise above B and the positive ground-impact root give height and flight time.

entries.model: Projectile from 3 m above water at 10 m/s and 25°.
derivation: The positive root of 0=3+10sin25°·t-gt²/2 gives t; horizontal distance is 10cos25°·t.

entries.model: Spring energy becomes gravitational potential plus muzzle kinetic energy, then projectile motion.
derivation: The ball travels 0.60 m along the 30° barrel (150 mm compression plus 450 mm to the muzzle), rising 0.30 m.
kv² bookkeeping: kx²/2=mgh+mv_C²/2 gives v_C=7.097 m/s.
Launch height is 0.60 m; solve the projectile ground-impact root and use L=v_Ccos30°·t.

entries.model: Projectile from height 1.8 m at 12 m/s and 40°.
derivation: Solve 0=1.8+12sin40°·t-gt²/2, then resolve impact velocity and range.

entries.model: B is the apex 40 m from launch; the far roof edge C is 60 m away.
derivation: At the apex, x=v₀cos60°·(v₀sin60°/g)=40, giving v₀=30.4 m/s.
H=(v₀sin60°)²/(2g)=34.65 m and v_B=v_x=15.2 m/s.
For the minimum clearing speed, impose the trajectory height H at x=60 m.

entries.model: The specified point is the apex at x=25 m and y=20 m.
derivation: Angle and magnitude follow from the two components; at the apex only v_x remains.

entries.model: Standard equal-height range and a horizontal throw matched to that range.
derivation: R=v²sin90°/g=14.679 m; flight time=2v sin45°/g=1.730 s; H=v²sin²45°/(2g)=3.670 m.
For a horizontal throw at 12 m/s with the same range, t=R/12 and H=gt²/2.
entries.result: R=14.68 m; t=1.73 s; H_max=3.67 m; horizontal-launch height=0.50 m

entries.model: Apex occurs 6 s after a 45° launch.
derivation: v₀sin45°=g·6, so v₀=83.24 m/s for g=9.81, not 114.1 m/s.
Then H=(g·6)²/(2g)=176.58 m, x=v₀cos45°·6=353.16 m, and apex speed=58.86 m/s.
A vertical launch with that same speed reaches y=v₀·6-g·6²/2=322.97 m.
entries.result: v₀=83.24 m/s; H=176.58 m; x=353.16 m; v_apex=58.86 m/s; vertical-launch y=322.97 m
entries.comparison_note: Owner review confirms the repository solution is correct. The key's 114.1 m/s and dependent values do not satisfy an apex exactly 6 s after launch at 45° with g=9.81.

entries.model: Evaluate the projectile at the fence x=5 m and compare with fence height; then repeat for a horizontal launch.
derivation: For 20°, t=5/(15cos20°)=0.3547 s and y=1.2+15sin20°·t-gt²/2=2.403 m, so the ball hits the 3 m fence while ascending.
For a horizontal launch, fence time is 0.333 s; ground time √(2·1.2/g)=0.4946 s, so it reaches the fence at y=0.655 m.
entries.result: 20°: t=0.3547 s, ascending, hits fence at 2.403 m; horizontal: hits fence at 0.655 m

entries.model: Constant acceleration from rest plus Newton's second law.
derivation: F-T=ma, so F=350a+120.

entries.model: One-dimensional impulse under a constant opposing force.
derivation: a=-F/m=-2 m/s² and v=0.5+a·3.
entries.result: v=-5.5 m/s, i.e. 5.5 m/s opposite the original direction

entries.model: Locked-wheel braking: a=-μg; average friction power equals friction work divided by time.
derivation: t=(v_f-v_i)/a=1.69895 s and P_avg=μmgd/t=163.70 kW.

entries.model: The displacement is down the incline. For each force use W=Fs cosγ, where γ is the angle between that force and the displacement.
derivation: The angles with the displacement are γ_N=90°, γ_f=180°, γ_G=50°, and γ_Q=50°.
The normal force is N=Gcos40°-Qsin50°=30.64 N; therefore f=μN=9.19 N.
The individual works are W_N=0, W_f=-13.79 J, W_G=192.84 J, and W_Q=154.27 J.
entries.comparison_note: Owner-authorized visual review of the handwritten solution confirms the force directions, individual works, and answer-key total.

entries.model: At constant speed, motor power equals resistive force times speed.
derivation: Required force is 2000(sin40°+0.25cos40°)=1668.6 N.
Path length for a 5 m rise is 5/sin40°=7.778 m; work is 12975.9 J.
entries.comparison_note: Owner review confirms the repository solution is correct. The answer key's 0.433 s is incompatible with the printed 0.5 kW power and 2 kN load.

entries.model: Measure acceleration from the timed descent, then resolve gravity and friction along the incline.
derivation: Incline length is h/sin30°=2 m and a=2s/t²=3.1888 m/s².
a=g(sin30°-μcos30°), giving μ=0.202; bottom speed is at=3.57 m/s.

entries.model: Two coupled bodies on perpendicular inclines; assume the printed arrow direction positive.
derivation: Write T-W₁sin37°-μW₁cos37°=(W₁/g)a for body 1.
Write W₂sin53°-μW₂cos53°-T=(W₂/g)a for body 2 and solve simultaneously.
entries.result: a=-2.76 m/s² (opposite the assumed arrow); T=47.03 N

entries.model: Energy from B to C and constant-acceleration motion on AB and CD.
derivation: From rest on AB, S=v_B²/(2·3)=35.36 m.
On CD the braking acceleration is -0.25g, so S₁=v_C²/(2·0.25g)=3.26 m.

entries.model: Resolve gravity and kinetic friction opposite uphill motion.
derivation: Use v²=v₀²+2as for v=5 m/s and again for v=0.

entries.model: Use kinematics to get acceleration, then Newton's second law along the incline.
derivation: F-Wsin20°-0.2Wcos20°=(W/g)a gives F=4840.9 N.
Total work equals ΔK=(W/2g)(3²-6²)=-13761.5 J; without F, Wsin20° exceeds maximum friction, so it slides down.
entries.result: F=4840.9 N; ΣW=-13761.5 J; body slides down if F is removed

entries.model: As in 6.7, apply Newton's law using measured deceleration.
derivation: F-Wsin15°-0.3Wcos15°=(W/g)a gives F=6032.7 N.
At rest Wsin15°<0.3Wcos15°, so static friction can hold it.
entries.result: F=6032.7 N; body remains at rest after F is removed

entries.model: Locked-wheel braking on a 6% grade.
derivation: With α=arctan0.06, uphill deceleration magnitude is g(sinα+μcosα).
Downhill braking magnitude is g(μcosα-sinα); use s=v²/(2|a|) at 105 km/h.
entries.result: uphill stopping distance=65.81 m; downhill=80.44 m

entries.model: Impending motion: static friction is at its limiting value.
derivation: For A moving up a 30° plane, T=m_Ag(sin30°+0.2cos30°)=264.17 N.
For B moving right, P>T+0.3m_Bg=440.75 N.
entries.result: force diagrams specified; T=264.17 N; P>440.75 N

entries.model: Limiting equilibrium on each incline immediately before A rises and B descends.
derivation: For A, T=m_Ag(sin25°+0.3cos25°)=340.7 N.
For B, P+m_Bg sin37°=T+0.4m_Bg cos37°, giving P≈229.9 N.
entries.result: force diagrams specified; T≈340.7 N; P≥229.9 N

entries.model: Use separate free-body diagrams for A and B; choose the positive tangential direction down the 20° plane, where B is on the verge of sliding.
derivation: For A, N₁=m_Agcos20° and limiting friction is f₁=0.3N₁=55.31 N down the plane; therefore T=m_Agsin20°+f₁=122.41 N.
A transmits N₁ and f₁ to B through contact. Its cable tension does not act directly on B.
For B, the plane normal is N₂=m_Bgcos20°+N₁-Psin20°=(m_A+m_B)gcos20°-Psin20°.
Tangential equilibrium of B alone is Pcos20°+m_Bgsin20°=f₁+0.5N₂. The term m_Agsin20° must not be added to this B-only equation.
Solving gives P=(f₁+0.5(m_A+m_B)gcos20°-m_Bgsin20°)/(cos20°+0.5sin20°)=189.24 N.
As a cross-check, the whole-system equation Pcos20°+(m_A+m_B)gsin20°=T+0.5N₂ gives the same result only when the external cable tension T is retained.
entries.result: force diagrams specified; T=122.41 N; P_{min}=189.24 N
entries.comparison_note: Corrected after reinspection of the source diagram: 189.24 N agrees with the answer-key value 189.19 N within intermediate-value rounding.

entries.model: Spring energy minus friction work becomes kinetic energy.
derivation: Spring compression is 0.05 m, so E_s=0.5·200·0.05²=0.25 J.
The printed geometry gives 0.30 m total sliding while/after the spring opens; friction work is 0.1·5·0.30=0.15 J.
With m=G/g, mv_B²/2=0.10 J.

entries.model: Spring energy supplies both the 0.12 m lift inside the launcher and exit kinetic energy.
derivation: At exit, K=E_s-G·0.12=2.10 J, giving v=9.075 m/s.
At the apex all spring energy has become gravitational energy: H=E_s/G.

entries.model: Initial spring energy is dissipated by friction and converted to kinetic energy.
derivation: At final rest, 25=μmgs, hence s=1.416 m.
entries.result: v_B=1.642 m/s; total stopping distance s=1.416 m

entries.model: Spring energy minus friction over AB becomes kinetic energy.
derivation: Compression is 0.06 m: E_s=0.5·200·0.06²=0.36 J.
Friction work over AB=0.25 m is 0.1·8·0.25=0.20 J; m=8/9.81 kg.
Thus mv_B²/2=0.16 J.

entries.model: Mechanical energy for the spring; work-energy or Newton's law for friction stopping.
derivation: Smooth case: mv²/2=kx²/2, so x=√(1·2²/80)=0.2236 m.
Rough case: mv²/2=μmg·s, equivalently a=-μg and 0=v²+2as.
entries.result: spring compression=0.2236 m; friction stopping distance=0.8155 m

entries.model: Conservation of mechanical energy, followed by spring compression.
derivation: Drops A→B and A→C are 4.5 m and 3 m, so v_B=√(2g·4.5)=9.396 m/s and v_C=√(2g·3)=7.672 m/s.
At maximum compression, mv_C²/2=kx²/2.

entries.model: Energy on the smooth circular part, friction on BD, then spring energy.
derivation: A→B drop is 0.6 m, so v_B=√(2g·0.6)=3.431 m/s.
v_D²=v_B²-2μg·0.8 gives v_D=2.938 m/s.
After D friction is neglected: mv_D²/2=kx²/2.

entries.model: Spring energy becomes launch kinetic energy, then horizontal projectile motion.
derivation: Impact speed is √(v_A²+v_y²)=8.606 m/s at 54.47° below horizontal.
entries.comparison_note: Owner review confirms the repository solution is correct. The key's 10 m/s launch speed requires four times the printed spring energy; its impact speed and range inherit that error.

entries.model: Energy on the circular track, perfectly inelastic collision, the supplied variable-mass equation applied to either closed body, then friction stopping.
derivation: v_D=√(2gr)=9.9045 m/s, and momentum conservation gives u=m_Av_D/(m_A+m_C)=1.6508 m/s.
For the closed body C, Δm=0 in the supplied formula F_EX=mΔV/Δt-V_relΔm/Δt, so F_EX=m_CΔV_C/Δt=50·1.6508/0.05=1650.8 N.
The same contact-force magnitude follows for A: m_A(v_D-u)/0.05=1650.8 N; stopping distance is u²/(2μg)=0.463 m.
entries.comparison_note: Owner review confirms the repository solution is correct. The key's 3300 N is the sum of the magnitudes of the equal and opposite action-reaction forces, not one force between the bodies. The owner-supplied formula gives 1650.8 N because Δm=0 for either closed body.

entries.model: Energy, inelastic momentum conservation, then spring compression.
derivation: At maximum compression, (m_A+m_C)u²/2=kx²/2.

entries.model: Energy, perfectly inelastic collision and friction stopping.
Gravity plus changing spring energy, then inelastic collision and final spring energy.
derivation: From A to B the body drops 0.6 m; the spring changes from length √(0.6²+0.3²) to its free 0.3 m length. Energy gives v_A=3.90 m/s.
Sticking collision gives u=2·3.90/3=2.60 m/s.
The final spring extension follows 3u²/2=50(l-0.3)²/2; geometry gives d=√(l²-0.3²).
entries.result: v_A=3.90 m/s; u=2.60 m/s; final spring length=0.937 m; d=0.888 m

entries.model: Energy down the smooth track, inelastic capture by the cart, then spring compression.
Direct full-path work-energy balance from rest at A to final rest, cross-checked by a two-stage balance at B.
derivation: The tangent angle α=30° is also the central angle of arc AB; its length is Rα and its height gain is R(1-cosα).
From A to final rest, ΔK=0 and friction is absent, so T·Rα=mg[R(1-cosα)+Ssinα].
Solving gives S=[T·Rα/(mg)-R(1-cosα)]/sinα=168.03 m; the two-stage calculation through K_B gives the same result.
The key value is exactly T·Rα/(mg sinα)=192.146 m, which omits the gravitational potential-energy gain on arc AB.
entries.comparison_note: The key's 192.146 m exactly reproduces T·Rα/(m·g·sinα), so it omits the 12.058 m height gain and corresponding gravitational work on arc AB. The printed data give S=168.03 m.

entries.model: Energy to the valley bottom plus radial Newton's law.
derivation: At B, N-W=(W/g)v_B²/R.

entries.model: At detachment N=0; combine radial dynamics with energy.
derivation: v²=v₀²+2gR(1-cosφ).
At N=0, mgcosφ=mv²/R; eliminating v gives cosφ=(2g+v₀²/R)/(3g).

entries.model: Energy from A to B and radial dynamics at the bottom.
derivation: N-W=(W/g)v_B²/R.

entries.model: Energy to point B and radial dynamics on the inside of the circular guide.
derivation: The height drop is 0.6-0.15sin45°=0.4939 m, so v_B=√(2gΔh)=3.11 m/s.
Along the inward radius, N+mgcos45°=mv_B²/R.

entries.model: Horizontal projectile over a 35 m vertical drop and 100 m horizontal gap.
derivation: At B, v_y=-gt; resolve magnitude and direction.

entries.model: Conservation of energy with g=10 m/s², then the no-loss-of-contact condition at C.
derivation: At the top of the hump, minimum contact has N=0, so mg=mv_C²/R.

entries.model: Energy on AB, friction work on BC, then horizontal projectile motion.
derivation: v_C²=v_B²-2μgd gives v_C=5.775 m/s.
From 4 m, t=√(8/g)=0.903 s; resolve impact velocity and use a=v_Ct.

entries.model: Energy to the horizontal takeoff, then projectile motion to the lower ground.
derivation: The A→B drop is 30-4=26 m, so v_B=√(2g·26)=22.586 m/s.
The landing is 4+20sin30°=14 m below B, so t=√(28/g)=1.689 s.
Subtract the ramp's horizontal projection 20cos30° from v_Bt to obtain d.

entries.model: Energy from A to B, then a 60° projectile from height 0.5 m.
derivation: Solve 0=0.5+v_Bsin60°·t-gt²/2 and use S=v_Bcos60°·t.

entries.model: Energy to B, friction to C, then horizontal projectile motion tangent to a 45° incline at D.
derivation: Parallel impact requires |v_y|=v_x, hence t=v_C/g.
Then h=gt²/2=v_C²/(2g) and a=v_Ct=v_C²/g.
